title: The Disparate Benefits of Deep Ensembles
reviewed_version: PMLR 267 published version fetched from supplied mlresearch source URL
summary: Four Major findings: signed fairness interpretation, inconsistent main experimental summaries/released analysis, resampled controlled inputs, and mismatched member scores in face HPP; one Minor invalid Bayesian likelihood identity.
limitations: Current source does not establish historical experimental provenance.
No author code executed or imported; no datasets/checkpoints/raw predictions reproduced.
Complete static reading limited to named core files/notebooks; other ancillary implementations not audited.
All source figures viewed qualitatively, not digitized.
Patient overlap and interpolation-sweep implementation not established.

problems.claim: Signed SPD/EOD decreases can be wrongly interpreted as less disparity.
problems.evidence: Gap -.019 to -.027 has signed change-.008 but absolute violation increases.008; visible1-EOD>1 and current metric defaults confirm sign issue.
problems.alternative_explanation: Positive-gap cases and absolute AOD may retain evidence for some disparate benefits.
problems.dependency: Task-wise fairness direction and significance interpretation.
problems.repair: Fix group identities, compute absolute violations per run, and regenerate statements and tests.

independent_verification.source_claim: Read definitions Eq5-7 and Table1 physical p4. Actually viewed Figure9 p19 and Table10 p27: race/gender EOD plot is above1 on the 1-EOD axis; before-HPP magnitudes .019/.027 conflict with treating negative signed change as reduced violation.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: metrics.py eod/spd defaults absolute=False while aod defaults True; original notebook JSON cell6 forms1-eod and plots it. A fixed advantageous-group name cannot impose a nonnegative rate difference across all targets and models.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The exact per-run absolute means and p-values are unavailable; because P2 also finds aggregation mismatches, the signed numbers are a compatible diagnostic, not a recovered raw run. Positive-gap cases and AOD can still support some disparate benefits.
independent_verification.core_dependency: Direction of task-wise fairness change is central quantitative evidence. Published definitions/axis contradict the universal nonnegative-violation interpretation.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained. State group ordering and signed directions separately; recompute absolute values per run and paired tests. Do not merely take an absolute value after averaging.

problems.claim: Main summaries disagree and released analysis mixes datasets, sizes and complements.
problems.evidence: FF age accuracy .812-.794=.018 not .022; current FF plot uses UTK accuracy; summary averages sizes; fairness delta subtractsF from1-F.
problems.alternative_explanation: Historical scripts likely differ; no claim the released complement bug generated the published small numbers.
problems.repair: Publish actual versioned scripts and paired run values; regenerate consistent datasets/ten-member summaries/tests.

independent_verification.source_claim: Read Table1 p4 caption explicitly referring to Table3 ten-member ensembles p18 and Table4 members p21, plus Table5 p26. Read original face cells6-8 and medical cell7 alongside preserved source transcription.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: Table3 FF age/gender .812,.190,.165,.126 and Table4 .794,.173,.153,.113 are same labelled quantities in stated captions. Three rounded numbers each to.001 permit at most.0015 arithmetic discrepancy. Table5 before-HPP accuracy .816 instead fits main .022 gain.

decisive_check.release_summary: np.mean over runs and all ensemble sizes

independent_verification.counterevidence: The complement error would produce large values unlike published small deltas, so it cannot be asserted as their actual origin. Different scripts/checkpoints/aggregation can explain the inconsistency but are not identified. Performance gains remain positive in the tabulated example.
independent_verification.core_dependency: Magnitude, dataset identity, aggregation and significance of main empirical results need one reproducible account. This is more than an isolated rounded cell.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained; identify historical source and paired runs, select size10 consistently, correct FF source and complement before regenerating summaries/tests.

problems.claim: Controlled evaluation changes the second input image between ensemble members for only one group.
problems.evidence: Fresh random same-label partner pergetitem, network-outer evaluation loop; identical function on differing views yields positive apparent DIV.
problems.alternative_explanation: Historical evaluation may have used fixed data; effects on trained values unmeasured.
problems.dependency: Controlled causal evidence for model-diversity mechanism.
problems.repair: Freeze shared evaluation inputs, separate view/model variation, rerun and control information-content changes.

independent_verification.source_claim: Read original controlled notebook cells2,6,9 and source6-7 Section6/Figure4 narrative. same_image=False draws a new same-label partner inside eachgetitem; evaluate loops over networks outside a new DataLoader and averages aligned indices.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: The same_image=False test group exists. Evaluation contains no shared realization cache or seed reset; seeding once earlier does not freeze successive random draws. Group0 receives identical fixed copies while group1 gets a varying second view.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Historical code could use fixed inputs and the actual numerical bias cannot be recovered. A model invariant to the changing image would not show this artifact; the issue is failure to isolate model variation, not inevitable positive bias in every metric.
independent_verification.core_dependency: Controlled support for a model-diversity mechanism in Section6/Figure4. Eq8 requires the same x across models; this implementation conflates test-view and parameter variation.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained. Materialize/hash common test inputs and recompute the first controlled experiment. Establish the separate interpolation-sweep/Table2 implementation before attributing this specific code defect to those results; information-content intervention also needs its own control.

problems.claim: Member-specific thresholds evaluated on member zero scores.
problems.evidence: Staticindexmem-to0mismatch; own two-member counterexample gives correct accuracies1,1 but mismatched1,.5.

independent_verification.source_claim: Read original face HPP notebook cells13/18: val_probits[m][mem] trains threshold, then ff/utk_test_probits[m][0] supplies evaluation scores through model.probits.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: The inner loop ranges over all mem. Scores are member-specific probability vectors; no explicit invariant makes all member0 scales equivalent. The first member matches, later members need not.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The example proves possible artificial degradation, not empirical direction or size; if members share suitable scales/predictions the effect can vanish. Historical source may differ, and medical HPP was not audited for this index error.
independent_verification.core_dependency: The ensemble-versus-member post-processing comparison supports the stated mitigation benefit; wrong member identity changes that comparison.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained despite a one-character potential fix: preserve member identity, match prediction records and rerun affected FF/UTK comparisons.

independent_verification.source_claim: Read AppendixC physical pp15-16 Eq12-15 and main Section6 Eq8. Eq15 attributes its approximation to sampled posterior integration but also interchanges log and expectation of the joint likelihood.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: A finite two-point posterior with weights1/2 and strictly positive likelihoods .9,.1 is valid. AtK1 both exact marginal likelihoods are.5, so there is no Monte Carlo error to explain the gap.

decisive_check.correct_identity: K*meanDIV = log(barp/p) + log E[L] - E[log L]

independent_verification.counterevidence: Eq8 remains exactly the mean member NLL minus ensemble NLL at common inputs. The empirical diversity diagnostic and experiments do not invoke Eq15 as a theorem certifying their causal effect. The exact equality can hold for constant joint likelihood but that assumption is absent.
independent_verification.core_dependency: An invalid Bayesian ratio interpretation, not the defining NLL identity. The bounded Minor assessment rests on this dependency analysis, not appendix location or ease of repair.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Minor retained. Replace the interpretation with the identity including the joint Jensen gap and fix Eq11 to P(X|Y,A)P(Y|A)=P(Y|X,A)P(X|A). No claim that changing an approximation sign alone fixes it.
